intervention: Five-morning bright-light protocol in the studied winter context

moa.description: Retinal–raphe signalling and altered transporter availability were proposed; the trial did not establish the cellular mediator.
moa.evidenceQualification: Mechanistic hypotheses in the primary discussion, not demonstrated mediation.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Winter subgroup anterior-cingulate serotonin-transporter binding was 12% lower after light than inactive-ionizer placebo (n=10; p=0.002).
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Regional human transporter-binding endpoint concerns serotonergic reuptake; does not directly measure serotonin release.

evidenceSource.exposure: 10000 lux white light for 30 minutes at 07:00 on five mornings
evidenceSource.comparator: Inactive negative ionizer; four-week washout; randomised order, counterbalanced crossover

limitations.text: Winter PFC comparison p=0.64; exploratory regional results did not survive multiplicity correction.
Small healthy-adult seasonal subgroups; no general or clinical prescription.
Binding is not serotonin release; symptom-change correlations were not significant.
Cellular mediator not established; sleep-change correlations nonsignificant.

recordRole: Structured handoff of existing canonical admission; no new admission or score.
